texts.preamble: M/S.Unique Spices vs The Commissioner Of Customs on 29 January, 2019 Author: G.R.Swaminathan Bench: G.R.Swaminathan 1 Before The Madurai Bench Of Madras High Court Dated: 29.01.2019 Coram: The Honourable Mr.Justice G.R.Swaminathan WP(MD)Nos.997, 1023, 1027 and 1077 of 2019 and WMP(MD)Nos.831, 898, 863 and 865 of 2019 M/ s. Unique Spices, Rep.by its Managing Partner E.M.Shahid, 7/405, Kunjattukara, Edathala North, P.O Aluva, Eranakulam District, Kerala 683 561. ... Petitioner in all Vs. 1.The Commissioner of Customs, Custom House, New Harbour Estate, Tuticorin 628 004. 2.The Assistant Commissioner of Customs (Imports), Tuticorin 628 004. ... Respondents in all cases Prayer in WP(MD)No.997 of 2019 : Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, to issue a Writ of Manda to direct the respondents herein to release and allow clearance of goods totally 900 bags viz., 54.000 Mts., of Sri Lankan Original Areca Nuts imported vide Bill of Entry No.8751448 dated 05.11.2018 http://www.judis.nic.in 2 M/S.Unique Spices vs The Commissioner Of Customs on 29 January, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67388083/ 1 on the basis of the Isfta Certificate issued by the Sri Lanka Competent Authority and as per the Fssai Certificate issued. Prayer in WP(MD)No.1023 of 2019 : Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, to issue a Writ of Manda to direct the respondents herein to release and allow clearance of goods totally 900 bags viz., 54.000 Mts., of Sri Lankan Original Areca Nuts imported vide Bill of Entry No.8751447 dated 05.11.2018 on the basis of the Isfta Certificate issued by the Sri Lankan Competent Authority and as per the Fssai Certificate issued. Prayer in WP(MD)No.1027 of 2019 :
texts.facts: Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, to issue a Writ of Manda to direct the respondents herein to release and allow clearance of goods totally 600 bags viz., 36.000 MTS., of Sri Lankan Original Areca Nuts imported vide Bill of Entry No.8751443 dated 05.11.2018 on the basis of the ISFTA Certificate issued by the Sri Lankan Competent Authority and as per the FSSAI Certificate issued. The writ petitioner is an importer and trader of Areca/Betal Nuts. They had imported four consignments of Srilankan Areca nuts. The imports totally weigh 180.000 MTS., They were supplied by M/s.Central Traders and LMW Exporters of Srilanka. The consignments had landed in India on 05.11.2018. The writ petitioner filed the Bills of Entry on the same date. Admittedly, the first check was ordered on 07.11.2018 and carried out on 08.11.2018. The results of the first check indicated that the goods are as declared in the bills of entry. M/S.Unique Spices vs The Commissioner Of Customs on 29 January, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67388083/ 2 2.The specific allegation of the writ petitioner is that the respondents wanted the writ petitioner to get the goods released after being provisionally assessed. The writ petitioner was not willing to avail the said offer. According to him, the aforesaid imported cargo http://www.judis.nic.in is exempted from levy of customs duty as per the provisions of the Indo-Sri Lanka Free Trade Agreement (ISFTA). He therefore filed these writ petitions for directing the respondents to allow their clearance. 3.The said writ prayers are strongly opposed by the respondents. A detailed counter affidavit has been filed. The learned standing counsel appearing for the respondents had also filed a typed set of papers and he reiterated the contentions set out therein. He prayed for dismissal of these writ petitions. 4.The stand of the respondents is that the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence issued an Alert Circular No.34 of 2015 dated 30.12.2018. It came to their notice that some importers are indulging in fabrication of records falsely declaring the country of origin as Srilanka. Therefore, the DRI cautioned all the Customs Commissioners that where evidence comesforth to show that the imports are from 3rd country, action may be taken as per law. It also stated that in other cases, the imports may be provisionally http://www.judis.nic.in assessed and a bank guarantee equivalent to the differential duty obtained for securing revenue. Thereafter, the certificate of origin along with invoices and bills of lading should be referred to Director (ICD), CBEC for verification with Sri Lankan authorities. 5.Since the respondents are bound by the aforesaid circular, they have sent the petitioner's documents to the Director (International Customs Division), CBEC, New Delhi for verification. Subsequently, on a query received from the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence, they had also submitted a similar request to the Additional Director, D.R.I, Chennai. Both these authorities are cross- checking with their counterparts in Srilanka. Both these authorities are yet to hear from their Srilankan counterparts. The respondents have not yet received any response from the Director (International Customs Division), CBEC or the Additional Director, DRI, Chennai as to the genuineness of the documents in question and that is why the respondents are not in a position to release the cargo. http://www.judis.nic.in 6.This Court by order dated 25.01.2019 had directed the first respondent to file an affidavit setting out the timeline of the events. Pursuant to the said direction, the first respondent has filed an affidavit dated 28.01.2019 in which the timeline has been set out. Paragraph No.12 of the said affidavit reads as under : Sl. Date Action/Result No. 1. 05.11.2018/ Bills of Entry filed online Monday 2 . 07.11.2018/ First Check Examination order online car M/S.Unique Spices vs The Commissioner Of Customs on 29 January, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67388083/ 3 3. 08.11.2018 / Customs Broker Produced the Cargo for First Thursday Check Examination before the Shed Officers. 4. 14.11.2018 / Examination of the cargo and the documents, Wednesday forwarded the sample for NOC from Plant Quarantine and Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) and subsequently transmitted the First Check Examination Report online 5. 16.11.2018 / File work initiated (Noting) Friday 6. 19.11.2018 / Permission granted for transferring and storing Monday the imported cargo in Domestic Containers. http://www.judis.nic.in 7. 27/ Letter addressed to Director (ICD), CBIC for 28.11.2018/ causing verification of genuineness of COO Thursday / (ISFTA Certificate) Wednesday 8. 29.11.2018 / The importer/petitioner was informed by way Thursday of query to furnish 100% Bank Guarantee for the duty exemption claimed on account of the COO/ISFTA and executing bond for the assessable value pending verification of the COO/ISFTA certificates. 9. 04.12.2018 / Reminder sent to Director(ICD), CBEC Tuesday 10. 12.12.2018 / Letter to the importer/petitioner to bond the Wednesday imported cargo under Sec.49 of the Customs Act, 1962 to avoid demurrage and in case of urgency provisional assessment may be resorted to on execution of necessary Bond and furnishing of 100% Bank Guarantee as per Circular No.38/2016-Customs dated 22.08.2016 11. 20.12.2018 / Relevant import documents sent to Additional Tuesday Director, DRI Chennai as requested over phone. 12. 24.12.2018 / The importer permitted to bond the imported Monday goods under Sec.49 of the Customs Act, 1962. http://www.judis.nic.in 7.This Court considered the rival contentions. The cargo arrived on 05.11.2018. The petitioner filed the bill of entries on the same date. The first check examination conducted by the respondents did not reveal anything amiss. In fact, the letter dated 20.12.2018 sent to the Additional Director, DRI, Chennai reads as follows : In all these cases first check appraisal was ordered for the said cargo with a direction to examine 100% of the cargo to examine and ensure from the goods or packaging that the goods have actually originated in the declared country of origin in terms of relevant rules and to check the declaration of the importer thoroughly vis-a-vis description, quantity and exemption claimed. Goods were examined and found to be as declared. In other words, even according to the first respondent, the goods were examined and found to be as declared. M/S.Unique Spices vs The Commissioner Of Customs on 29 January, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67388083/ 4 8.It must be noted that the Government of India has issued a detailed instruction vide Instruction No.31 of 2016 dated 12.09.2016 covering the same subject. Para No.2 of the said instruction issued http://www.judis.nic.in by the Ministry of Finance, Department of Revenue, Central Board of Excise & Customs, Government of India reads as under : 2.Rules of Origin are notified under each of the Agreements which require the importer to, inter alia, make a claim for preferential tariff at the time of importation, and submit a Certificate of Origin (COO) in the prescribed form. The Rules of Origin under the FTAs, as notified under Section 5(1) of the Customs Tarrif Act, 1975, provide for verifying the authenticity of the Certificates of Origin and also the information contained therein.
